We peeked at Jean's hives in the field.
She told us, “Each bee works hard.”

<<<page display="41" pdf="48">>>
Fish swim in lakes and creeks.
Fish swim in deep blue seas or
oceans.
Let's dive into the water. Let's
look at fish!

<<<page display="42" pdf="49">>>
Fish can swim alone. Fish can
swim with a partner.

Fish can swim in a bunch,
too. A bunch of fish is called a
school.

<<<page display="43" pdf="50">>>
A school has lots of fish.
They are a team.

The fish help each other. They
look for food together.

<<<page display="44" pdf="51">>>
Fish eat lots of things. Some
fish eat small animals. Some
fish eat other fish!

<<<page display="45" pdf="52">>>
It can be unsafe to swim alone.
What is the chief reason? Danger!
A fish can get snapped up!
But a fish can hide in a school.

<<<page display="46" pdf="53">>>
Fish in a school have a neat trick.
The fish swim close together.
Big fish will not mess with them
because they look like one
huge fish.
These crescent-tail
bigeye fish swim in a
school to fool big fish.
<<<page display="47" pdf="54">>>
This big fish wants to eat. But
it stays away. The school
looks like a huge fish that may
eat him!
